added_models.model: Pfizer guinea-pig tracheal-strip relaxation (slow M3 off-rate) and in vivo duration-of-action models

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig tracheal strips are named in the abstract; the in vivo species is not. PF-03635659 entered Phase 1 in 2008 (NCT00864786), so the model predates its 2011 publication; 2011 is the earliest public record.
engagement.quote: Compound 47 (PF-3635659) is identified as a Phase II clinical candidate from this series with in vivo duration of action studies confirming its potential for once-daily use in humans.
engagement.note: Guinea-pig tracheal-strip off-rate and in vivo duration picked PF-03635659 for once-daily dosing; no patient readout yet.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the model existed and was used for a member drug before any patient comparison was public.

engagement.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1 at 24 h; the model gave duration of airway smooth-muscle relaxation, not an FEV1 effect size
engagement.confidence_note: Registry tables only; no paper found for the trial. Single-dose, placebo- and tiotropium-controlled 5-way crossover in 22 moderate COPD patients; mean difference vs placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 +51, +79, +93 mL at 180, 580, 1450 ug (95% CI lower limits 6, 43, 56 mL); tiotropium +61 mL.
engagement.quote: Trough FEV1 was calculated as the average of the largest FEV1 value from 3 readings recorded at 24 hours (hrs) and 24.5 hrs post-dose.
engagement.note: One inhaled dose held trough (24-h) FEV1 51–93 mL above placebo in 22 COPD patients, as the duration model said.
engagement.judgement: FEV1 at 24 h is a downstream readout of the model's smooth-muscle relaxation and in vivo bronchoprotection. The model paper (2011) was already public, so the registry posting (2016-02-19) is the earliest public pairing (rule 6).

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig tracheal strips are named in the abstract; the in vivo species is not. PF-03635659 entered Phase 1 in 2008 (NCT00864786), so the model predates its 2011 publication; 2011 is the earliest public record.

dose.magnitude_basis: regimen: once-daily potential predicted from in vivo duration; 24-h trough FEV1 significant at 180–1450 ug after a single dose
dose.confidence_note: Registry tables only; no paper found for the trial. Single-dose, placebo- and tiotropium-controlled 5-way crossover in 22 moderate COPD patients; mean difference vs placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 +51, +79, +93 mL at 180, 580, 1450 ug (95% CI lower limits 6, 43, 56 mL); tiotropium +61 mL.
dose.quote: Trough FEV1 was calculated as the average of the largest FEV1 value from 3 readings recorded at 24 hours (hrs) and 24.5 hrs post-dose.
dose.note: Once-daily target reached: a single 180–1450 µg dose kept trough FEV1 51–93 mL over placebo at 24 h (tiotropium +61 mL).
dose.short: Once-daily target reached at every dose
dose.judgement: The model's regimen claim was once-daily potential; a single dose held FEV1 at 24 h at every dose tested, so the target was reached and sufficient. The abstract states a design aim of low systemic exposure but no tolerated-dose margin, so margin_stated is false; the program's later discontinuation is unexplained in any source found and is not a dose failure.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1 vs placebo; the model predicted 24-h bronchodilation, not an effect size
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry tables only; no paper found for the trial. Single-dose, placebo- and tiotropium-controlled 5-way crossover in 22 moderate COPD patients; mean difference vs placebo in change from baseline trough FEV1 +51, +79, +93 mL at 180, 580, 1450 ug (95% CI lower limits 6, 43, 56 mL); tiotropium +61 mL.
efficacy.quote: Trough FEV1 was calculated as the average of the largest FEV1 value from 3 readings recorded at 24 hours (hrs) and 24.5 hrs post-dose.

patient_trials.quote: Change From Baseline in Trough Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (FEV1)

efficacy.note: Primary trough FEV1 met at all three doses (+51/+79/+93 mL vs placebo, CI excluding zero); later dropped, reason unpublished.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on the pre-specified primary (change from baseline trough FEV1); all three doses beat placebo with confidence intervals excluding zero. Phase 2A, single dose, n=22, so medium confidence. The model predicted a surrogate only; no outcome trial applies.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Patient-side AE data are registry tables only (NCT01033487, posted 2016-02-19).
safety.quote: Together, these attributes minimize systemic exposure following inhalation, mitigate potential drug-drug interactions, and reduce systemically mediated adverse events.
safety.note: Series designed to minimise systemic exposure and systemic adverse events; no quotable patient-side safety comparison for PF-03635659.
safety.judgement: The series paper states a low-systemic-AE prediction. NCT01033487's AE table (n=22, single dose) lists no dry mouth or other systemic antimuscarinic event on PF-03635659 arms and one serious AE on tiotropium, but the registry carries no quotable sentence and the exposure is one dose, so by rule 3 the cell stays untested.

added_models.model: Human isolated bronchial tissue: carbachol-evoked contraction, potency and washout offset (Theravance)

engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the quoted passage is an IND review memo (Reference ID 3458706, IND 119,840) embedded in the NDA pharmacology review, written before the 28-day Protocol 0117 (NCT02040792, start 2014-05); the sponsor's ex-vivo study number and date are not in the bundle, so the model may be older. Peer-reviewed report is Hegde 2018 (doi 10.1002/prp2.400).
engagement.quote: The sponsor provided ex vivo pharmacodynamic (PD) data to show a dose-dependent antagonism of ACh and carbachol-induced contractions in rat tracheal tissue (3 – 100 nM TD-4208) and human bronchial tissue (1 – 1000 nM TD-4208), respectively.
engagement.note: Ex-vivo human bronchi showed concentration-dependent antagonism of carbachol contraction, filed under the IND before Phase 2b; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the earliest documented use. Dated to the IND memo rather than the 2018 paper because the FDA text shows the tissue data were in hand before the dose-ranging trial; this is therefore not a retrodiction.

engagement.magnitude_basis: duration: tissue washout offset t1/2 >10 h vs 24-h trough FEV1 bronchodilation in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Open access (PMC5927803, online 2018-04-30); full text read. The paper's clinical side is the Phase 2 dose-range studies (NCT02040792 results 2016-12-07; NCT01704404 results 2017-03-13). Hyphens in the quote are ASCII where the PMC XML uses U+2010.
engagement.quote: The findings from these translational studies are consistent with emerging clinical data showing 24 hours bronchodilatory activity of nebulized revefenacin in COPD patients.
engagement.note: Slowly reversible antagonism in human bronchi (offset t1/2 >10 h) matched 24-h bronchodilation after once-daily nebulized revefenacin in COPD patients.
engagement.short: Tissue offset >10 h, patients bronchodilated 24 h
engagement.judgement: The paper itself sets the human-tissue offset beside the Phase 2 24-h FEV1 data, so comparison_stated is true. FEV1 is a downstream readout of M3 blockade in airway smooth muscle. Dated to the 2018-04-30 online publication, the first public pairing.

dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the quoted passage is an IND review memo (Reference ID 3458706, IND 119,840) embedded in the NDA pharmacology review, written before the 28-day Protocol 0117 (NCT02040792, start 2014-05); the sponsor's ex-vivo study number and date are not in the bundle, so the model may be older. dose.magnitude_basis: regimen: once-daily implied by the tissue offset; once-daily nebulized dosing gave sustained 24-h bronchodilation
dose.confidence_note: Open access (PMC5927803, online 2018-04-30); full text read. The paper's clinical side is the Phase 2 dose-range studies (NCT02040792 results 2016-12-07; NCT01704404 results 2017-03-13). Hyphens in the quote are ASCII where the PMC XML uses U+2010.
dose.quote: Indeed, clinical Phase 2 dose-range studies have demonstrated sustained 24 hours bronchodilation in COPD patients following once-daily dosing.
dose.note: Once-daily regimen implied by the >10 h tissue offset was reached: once-daily nebulized dosing gave sustained 24-h bronchodilation in Phase 2.
dose.judgement: The tissue model gives a duration, not an exposure; its regimen claim (once-daily) is what patients tested. Isolated bronchi cannot state a tolerability margin, so margin_stated is false and the toxic end of the window is left to the rat antisialagogue track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: trough FEV1; the tissue model predicted sustained bronchodilation, not an effect size
efficacy.confidence_note: Open access (PMC5927803, online 2018-04-30); full text read. The paper's clinical side is the Phase 2 dose-range studies (NCT02040792 results 2016-12-07; NCT01704404 results 2017-03-13). Hyphens in the quote are ASCII where the PMC XML uses U+2010.
efficacy.reason: Airflow improved as tissue antagonism predicted
efficacy.quote: Indeed, clinical Phase 2 dose-range studies have demonstrated sustained 24 hours bronchodilation in COPD patients following once-daily dosing.

patient_trials.quote: At day 85, revefenacin 88 µg and 175 µg improved trough FEV1 versus placebo in Study 0126 (by 79 mL [p=0.0003] and 146 mL [p<0.0001]) and Study 0127 (by 160 mL and 147 mL; both p<0.0001).
Revefenacin, administered once daily for 12 weeks to patients with moderate to very severe COPD, demonstrated clinically significant improvements in trough FEV1 and OTE FEV1.

efficacy.note: Primary trough FEV1 met in Phase 2b (day 28) and both 12-week Phase 3 trials; tissue model predicted bronchodilation only.
efficacy.short: Trough FEV1 primary met, as predicted
efficacy.judgement: Hegde's stated comparison is to the Phase 2 24-h bronchodilation; the pre-specified primaries (day-28 trough FEV1 in NCT02040792, day-85 trough FEV1 in both Phase 3 trials) were all met, so same. The model predicted a surrogate only; no outcome trial applies. The NCT02040792 paper (Pudi 2017) was not read, so its quote is left null.

considered_not_added: AstraZeneca guinea-pig bronchoconstriction/duration/systemic side-effect models for AZD8683 (Mete 2013, doi 10.1016/j.bmcl.2013.09.092): the same system as the draft's az-guinea-pig-bronchoprotection track, so not a new track. For that track's owner: NCT01205269 results 2013-11-13 (primary peak and 22-26 h FEV1; registry AE table lists zero events in all three arms) and NCT01708057 results 2013-09-30 (terminated).

Human challenge models: none used by any member. NCT00864786 (PF-03635659 Phase 1) read salivary flow and spirometry in healthy men, not a bronchoconstrictor challenge; NCT01419600 (AZD8683 single ascending dose) is safety only; NCT00568503 (QAX028 single-dose PoC) is a COPD patient trial with no posted results.

Recombinant hM2/hM3 CHO-cell kinetic-selectivity and radioligand off-rate assays (Hegde 2018): in-vitro receptor assays with no patient comparison of their own; described alongside the human-bronchus track rather than tracked.

Revefenacin population pharmacokinetic model (2021, doi 10.1007/s40262-020-00938-3): built from patient trial data after the fact, not a model system that predicted a patient result; no prospective in-silico or QSP dose selection found for any member.
In-vitro nebulizer lung-deposition study of once-daily LAMAs (2022, doi 10.1177/17534666221077561): device aerosol characterisation, no patient comparison.
QAX028 and CHF5992: no model paper in Europe PMC under either code; NCT01068613 has no results; the only CHF hit (NCT01584505) is CHF5993 triple therapy, not CHF5992.
Patient-derived organoids, PDX co-clinical, ex-vivo drug-sensitivity and human genetic (CHRM3 loss-of-function) models: no use found for any member; the class is scored at class level only.

THRX-195518 (revefenacin metabolite) rat isolated trachea study (PharmR 07-195518-PH-04): metabolite characterisation, no patient comparison; the parent's rat/dog in vivo work is already the draft's revefenacin-rat-dog-bronchoprotection track.
